newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors buying protection.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors buying protection.

text.p: Trading in major U.S. index options cooled a bit on Tuesday, and with the market holding fairly steady after Monday's sharp rally, investors were buying puts for downside protection, traders said.
By 1200 CDT/1700 GMT, put volume in the S&P 100 index was 89,761 compared to call volume of 54,451.
The pattern was similar in the S&P 500 .SPX, where puts outpaced calls by 61,692 to 24,087.
"I think we're back up in that area where that's protective puts more than anything else," a trader in Chicago said of the heavy put volume.
"The market is up so high that people are just thinking, 'if it does go down, I need something to protect my gains,'" the trader said.
In afternoon trading, the bellwether Dow industrial average .DJI was up 40 points at 7,255 after surging 143 points Monday.
Despite the Dow's gains, broader market measures lagged.
The SPX rose less than a point to 831 and June S&P 500 futures slipped about a point to 835.80.
The OEX was ahead about 2-1/4 points to nearly 815.
"We're not that busy," one OEX trader said, adding that activity on Monday was relatively modest until late in the session.
"We had a lot of screaming at the end of the day," he said.
Out-of-the-money puts both on Monday and Tuesday were holding steady even as the market moved on, he noted.
The most active OEX put was the May 790, which traded about 9,750 contracts. It was up 1/8 at 4-1/8.
Behind that, the May 770 traded about 8,750 and rose 1/4 to 2-1/8.
The most active OEX call was the May 810, which traded about 7,730 contracts and fell 1-5/8 to 14-1/2.
Traders said the weakness in June S&P 500 futures, despite the strong Dow industrials, helped keep volatility in OEX options on firm ground.
The CBOE's volatility index .VIX was up 0.75 at 23.02.
"The volatility's way up. People are not selling puts yet," a trader said. "They're still thinking maybe they'll nedd them in case this (rally) isn't for real.
"But it sure looks real," he said, adding that if bonds reverse course and move higher, stocks could climb further.
Other options traders agreed.
"We're not going down, especially if bonds start getting strong," the OEX trader said. "There's no bad news out there."
The June U.S. Treasury 30-year bond future was down 2/32 at 109-31 in afternoon trading.
"Once again, it looks like new highs especially if the bonds stay up," one trader said. "There's a lot of pent-up buying. People who missed the move still need to get in."
